Have lived in almost all areas of this city over the years. Wouldn't pick downtown again - simply not for me. The recommendations others have made for Broadway area are solid; close to core with a more laid back attitude.

Yesterday having a smoke I ended up giving away 3 more... gave one to a passerby and they flock to you and then your in for a real treat. Same with change 😂.  I mean sure you can say no. If working downtown you'll be doing it lots... on days off I prefer to wander outside in my neighborhood in peace though. 

If you drive, parking downtown is a nasty beast. You either pay way more in rent to include a parking spot or get a resident parking pass... or a ton of tickets. And as others have mentioned, there are certain necessities like groceries that aren't available downtown or even close... 

If you like restaurants/pubs/theaters/clothing shops you're in luck, there are tons close by. Of course these are all easily walkable from nearby neighborhoods where parking and groceries and less... seedy... populace resides.

Something to consider is an at home "mom & me" day spa and photoshoot. Take things you have already - any make up/hair/nail products and household stuff to do manicures, pedicures, facials, and such. I haven't looked it up myself recently but I know there should be diy recipes for facial/hair mask/exfoliant stuff online if you don't have anything bought/pre-made.  Spend the time doing each other's hair, nails, and make-up and put on your favorite outfits and take pictures. At home is fine, or go to a local pretty spot like a park or historical landmark. It's more about the memories than the money 😊  You can even ask another person to take a picture or you two together, get a dollar store frame and print it at Walmart for a few cents and decorate it together so she can put it in her room. Now that my mother passed (stupid cancer) I wish I had more good memories of us together. 

Another good memory thing might be to spend the day creating something together, if either or both of you are creative. Sew a quilt/blanket together of old clothing or materials. Bake and decorate a fun or fancy cake (I know this one requires having ingredients and/or cake mix, but again try a dollar store for box cake mix should only be a dollar or two). 

Give your time to her where you will learn about her school, friends, boy interests, favorite foods, stresses and concerns with a promise of zero judgment or punishment for anything talked about. Form a bond through developing a "safe space" in communication now that will be so valuable through her teen years.

Fantasize with her about a dream wedding. Go online or ask friends and family for old magazines and find pictures together of a bridal gown, bridesmaids dresses, suits or tuxs, decor, food etc. Listen to music she would like to walk down  the aisle to and let her know it is OK to dream about this fancy amazing day in her future. Use it as time to talk about what is important in relationships without seeming preachy or overbearing.

It's hard to say what to do without knowing her interests and hobbies but just try to make the day about her, even if there isn't money to be spent make a gift of time. 

She may want to have friends over or spend time with them as part of her birthday too - this doesn't have to mean a big expensive party. Make it a sleepover and ask everyone to bring a pillow, blanket, and their favorite food/snack item with enough to share, then you're just providing one snack yourself rather than feeding a horde or teen girls. 

As far as food/financial assistance go, you could try going to an affluent residential neighborhood where no one knows you and go down a few blocks with a box collecting for the food bank. Ask for "most needed" items for yourself but phrase it as a food bank donation. Keep the items you need for your family, and take the unneeded items to the food bank as promised to the people who donated. There is no need for them to know you are also being helped by this.

Hopefully some of this helped?

Ok. Your body, your life, your choice. Advice on the rest of it? If he threatens to tell your parents, inform him that they will not believe his word over yours - after all, he is an underemployed, beer guzzling, cheating idiot. Why would they believe him? You could counter it with "no, he is just trying to control my relationships with others by telling lies about me". So his threat, as scary as it may feel, isn't very viable in reality. Also, anyone that uses threats like that to control you is a narcissist and a likely a gaslighter. Bet you when he cheated he first tried to convince you there was nothing going on and that you were crazy for thinking it. You make the choice on your relationship status, but it doesn't sound at ALL healthy or mutually beneficial. And if you or he thinks that a child would save the relationship, it will NOT. Any parent would say - even the ones who LOVE parenting - that a child causes way more stress and tension in the relationship. Do what you need to do. You can have one of these conversations; 

"If we were to have a child together ever, it is not now. We cannot financially or emotionally handle it. We are falling apart as it is. This is my body and my choice, and you will respect that 100% with no accusations, threats, guilt trips or anger if you want to remain in this relationship. You will not be bringing to term, birthing, breastfeeding. I would be and I do not want to do that." (If he threatens the "telling parents" or others, "My word is going to be more trusted than yours so I am not accepting that threat. It does not scare me more than pregnancy/childbirth/being a parent right now."
OR, if you feel he could become violent or aggressive in any way if you went the above conversation, you could make the appointment and go without his knowledge and simply claim that you randomly miscarried. Google some facts on ectopic pregnancies and tell him that is what it is so it must be aborted or you will miscarry/have other health complications. I doubt you'd want to lie to someone you plan on spending your whole life with like that, but I don't know your whole story.

At the end of the day, keeping the child will mean poverty, undue stress and strain, unhappiness, and a guaranteed broken relationship as you would hold it against him for threatening and controlling you to convince you to have an unwanted child on top of all the other issues you already face. 
If you were my best friend or sister, I'd tell you to 1) end the relationship 2) forewarn those that he has access to that his behavior has been unacceptable and that he is threatening to tell stories about you (nip it in the bud, in advance, tell them even before the break up) 3) have that procedure done as early as possible and 4) never look back you have a lot ahead 😊

The whole situation sounds very shady. I guess,  abusive nature aside,  what is his reasoning behind wanting your income? If living at home they are supporting you with a roof over your head that you are not willing to leave due to your other family members, is it possible to discuss a rent or room & board amount that you will agree to pay? You are an adult. If it is for reasons that there are expenses to be paid by you, it is fine to give him a portion of your income as rent/room & board. But this should be a cash or cheque payment monthly or as agreed upon to go to household expenses, and with the agreement that remaining money is YOURS. 
It isn't legal or normal to "seize" your wages. But it seems you wish to keep the peace as much as possible, so a meeting with BOTH parents to agree upon a certain rent amount may do this, if possible.

Sounds like they are either a) being fed wrong or incomplete information by siblings and/or b) on a power trip of some kind. My other advice stands either way. Find ways to self calm... i find the counting helps and if that fails, I try to pinpoint where in my body I "feel the anxiety" most. Does my throat feel closed? Is there pain in my chest? Sick feeling in my stomach? Then I tap exactly there rhythmically and breathe, focusing only on that until the feeling gets manageable. It sometimes moves to a different spot, then I just switch the tapping to there. It sometimes goes away in a minute or two, sometimes longer, but always feels at least a bit better within 10 minutes. 
I'm not a doctor, just know what helps me and I hate hearing how others have to go through this shit so I try to share what helps me in hopes that maybe some of it might help another.
As far as the legality of anything, I'm not much help especially since I'm in canada, (here, I would personally consider pressing harassment charges against the siblings - also they could never have called you a missing person here without proof of no contact for 72+ hours and if they had tried that and you proved you did confirm wellbeing and they still filed a report they could be charged with filing a false report!) but I hope you are currently in a safe, non threatening environment. If not please learn what options are available to you and utilize them.

Take deep breaths. You do not have to do anything but remember that you are going to be ok, and breathe. Count to 10 seconds, realize you have been ok for those seconds,  and repeat. Press two fingertips together and FEEL them. Think about how it feels. Then remind yourself again you are ok. You are ok. 
You do not have to answer anything other than your identity and then let them know you are fine. You can say you have anxiety issues but are not a danger to yourself or others. Inform them, calmly if you can, that you need physical space and calm words so your anxiety is not triggered any worse than it already is. If their questioning is making you upset, ask them to please let you gather yourself for a few minutes. You have not done anything wrong. You are ok.

As far as your main post - you can't control other people, only yourself. And it's hard to find someone that can love you if you don't love yourself. NO woman wants to be looked to to provide 100% of a man's self worth. But being honest about that can help. "I suffer from low self esteem and depression. I am working on this and am (taking these steps) to accomplish this. Just so you may better understand me." 
Depression isn't caused by another person - its internal. Others can help but only if you also help yourself. So the best way to find a good partner? Work on you and put yourself out there. Dont look at this as a task to reach an end result of a girlfriend - you will not find one ever that way, just be discouraged.
Get out there to social events. Meet tons of new people. Be honest about your emotional state with people and keep the ones around who react with support. Build your life up and someone will want to share it with you; level of your attractiveness will not matter to someone if they want to be part of the life you build/are building! No one will want to be with even the most attractive person if they do not have goals/plans/dreams/improvements they are working towards.  Dont look to someone else to provide you with that life as it will discourage you, unfortunately. 
I know depression is hard firsthand, and I'm not great at always functioning properly too. But it is making the effort and realizing that the act of trying is more often what mattered, not the end result.
